tagline: From the Palace of the Governors through forest to the ski basin
intro: The Santa Fe National Forest Scenic Byway runs 15 miles from the Palace of the Governors through aspen and evergreen forest to the Santa Fe Ski Basin. NM 475 provides the climb into the Sangre de Cristo Mountains. The New Mexico Tourism Department promotes the byway for its mountain and badlands views and opportunities for hiking, skiing and picnicking. The drive passes through Hyde Memorial State Park, whose stone-and-log lodge is one of the route’s built landmarks. Farther up, the ski basin sits in alpine forest near tree line, with its base reached directly by NM 475.

The upper destination began taking shape in 1936, when a rope tow powered by a Packard sedan engine was installed at the future resort site. In 1949, the Sierras de Santa Fe group founded the ski basin and raised money for its first chairlift. The resort now occupies alpine forest near tree line.

Begin downtown at the Palace, then follow the mountain road through Hyde Memorial State Park. Its stone-and-log lodge stands along a route with trailheads, picnic areas and views toward the Arroyo Seco badlands. Beyond the park, continue to the ski basin above 10,000 feet. NM 475 ends there, rather than crossing the mountain range.

moments.title: Palace of the Governors
moments.text: The adobe Palace of the Governors served as New Mexico’s seat of government until 1901. It housed Spanish colonial government, then the administration of the Mexican province, and later the first U.S. territorial capitol. Its later museum life required restoration: Jesse L. Nusbaum took charge of that work in 1909 and completed it in 1913. The Palace housed the state history museum from 1909 to 2009. The New Mexico History Museum opened beside it in 2009. The building faces the Santa Fe Plaza on Palace Avenue, between Lincoln and Washington avenues, within the Santa Fe Historic District.

moments.title: Hyde Memorial State Park
moments.text: The byway jogs through Hyde Memorial State Park beside a lodge built of stone and logs. The park lies eight miles northeast of Santa Fe in the Sangre de Cristo Mountains. Hiking and camping are summer activities here; snow-covered hillsides draw people for tubing in winter.
moments.notice: Notice the lodge’s stone-and-log construction along the byway.

moments.title: Ski Santa Fe
moments.text: NM 475 ends at Santa Fe Ski Basin, in alpine forest near tree line. The resort spreads across Lake Peak and Tesuque Peak, with runs descending toward the base in a fan shape. Its early lift was a rope tow installed in 1936 and powered by a Packard sedan engine. The Sierras de Santa Fe group raised money for a chairlift when it founded the basin in 1949. The following year, Joe Juhan bought the basin and skier Ernie Blake managed it. In winter, snowfall draws cross-country skiers and snowshoers to backcountry trails, while downhill skiers and snowboarders use the resort’s groomed slopes.
